title: Probabilistic KV quantization + memory-fragmentation experiments and dynamic fallback policy
creator: Maya Lin
description: Investigate a probabilistic, per-shard KV quantization strategy that adapts encoding format (FP8/INT8/INT4) dynamically based on cohort sensitivity, continuous batching behavior, and GPU memory fragmentation. Goal: reduce GPU memory use for long-context workloads while bounding quality regressions and maintaining tail latency SLOs. Deliver an evaluation matrix, a runtime prototype for dynamic format switching and fallback, and an A/B rollout plan for Dedicated and Hosted lanes.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Prototype implements per-shard format tags with on-the-fly conversion paths and a fast fallback to full-precision cache entries.
2) Experimental evaluation across defined cohorts (long-context summarization, code generation, factual QA) with token-level KL and end-task metrics showing <= 2% degradation for chosen default profile vs baseline FP16, and P95 latency within 10% of baseline under production batching distributions.
3) Memory reduction documented (GB saved / shard and end-to-end on common instance types), and rollout playbook covering canary ranges, abort criteria, and monitoring queries for quality regressions.
experiment_plan:
Overview:
- Implement two orthogonal mechanisms: (A) probabilistic encoding where a shard is stored in a compact format with a configured probability p (e.g., 0.25/0.5/0.75) to enable stochastic exposure across requests; (B) deterministic cohort-aware encoding where shard formats are chosen based on prompt cohort sensitivity scores computed offline.
- Provide an in-runtime fallback: if model output fails soft-quality gates (measured by cheap proxy like top-k logit deviation or token-level KL on next-token distribution), re-run using the uncompressed shard or a higher-fidelity format.\nKernel/allocator work:
- Experiment with buddy allocator tuning and defragmentation triggers when switching formats to avoid OOMs during conversion.
- Coordinate with continuous-batching scheduler to avoid mixing heavy-format-conversion requests in a single GPU batch (schedule conversions during low-utilization micro-batches).
\nWork items (rough):
1) Instrument shard metadata and serialization versioning (ENG-90123.1)
2) Implement compact encoders/decoders for INT4 and FP8 with block-aligned layout (ENG-90123.2)
3) Add probabilistic write path + cohort selector (ENG-90123.3)
4) Fast fallback path that swaps in-materialized shard slices with zero-copy where possible (ENG-90123.4)
5) Allocator tuning and fragmentation monitoring (ENG-90123.5)
6) Eval harness and dashboards (ENG-90123.6)
7) Canary/playbook + rollout automation (ENG-90123.7)
matrix:
Sweep axes:
- Formats: FP16 baseline, FP8-e4m3, INT8 symmetric, INT4 block-quant, hybrid (int4 keys + fp8 values)
- Probabilities: 0.0 (deterministic full), 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0 (always compact)
- Cohorts: long-context summarization (>=8k tokens), code generation (multi-file snippets), instruction-following short prompts, factual QA (closed-book)
- Batch distribution: production-like (P50=1 token/req, long-tail up to 512 tokens), stress distribution (high token throughput)
- Allocator strategies: no-defrag, synchronous defrag during low-utilization, incremental slab reclamation
\nWe will run each cell with 3 seeds and capture per-seed metrics. Total targeted experiments: ~180 cells x 3 = ~540 runs.
metrics:
Primary:
- Token-level symmetric KL between compressed vs FP16 next-token logits (averaged and P95)
- End-task quality: ROUGE-L / BLEU where applicable, and a small human-eval pass for worst-case prompts
- Latency: decode P50/P95/P99 and end-to-end request tail under realistic continuous batching
- Memory: peak per-GPU resident KV cache (GB) and transient overhead during conversion
- Re-run rate: fraction of requests triggering fallback and additional cost impact
Secondary:
- Model perplexity drift, top-5 token overlap, percent of outputs with structural corruption (for code), and cost per 1M tokens served extrapolated from measured throughput
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Compaction-triggered fragmentation causing OOMs during heavy conversions. Mitigation: conservative default p (0.25) for probabilistic writes and allocator defrag heuristics that trigger only under <70% GPU utilization. Also pre-reserve swap buffer memory for conversions.
Risk: Quality regressions for specific cohorts (e.g., code). Mitigation: cohort-aware deterministic mapping that pins these cohorts to higher-fidelity formats and a fast fallback that replays using full-precision cache if cheap proxy gate fails.
Risk: Increased P95 due to conversion latency during continuous batching. Mitigation: schedule conversions outside hot micro-batches and limit max concurrent conversions per-GPU.
notes_and_updates: 2025-02-10 - Created draft experiment plan and lined up owners for codec implementation (Ravi) and allocator work (Lena).
2025-02-18 - Implemented metadata tag for shards; landed proto for on-disk compact layout (PR: github.com/redwood/kv/PR-2476).

2025-02-24 - Early microbench: INT4 encode/decode is ~2.5x faster than full naive FP32 conversion but increases batch variance. Observed temporary 6% P95 latency noise. Scheduling mitigations planned.

2025-03-01 - Ran first cohort eval (summarization) for p=0.5 hybrid (int4 keys + fp8 values): token-KL median 0.015, P95 0.072; end-task ROUGE-L drop 1.3% vs FP16. Memory savings ~18% per large shard on A100-40GB. Adding fallback gate thresholds to reduce worst-case degradation.
2025-03-04 - Experiment infra stabilized; allocating runs for code cohort next week. Need SRE to approve defragmentation kernel flag for Dedicated staging clusters (ticket SRE-119).
